domain: environmental water quality / regulatory classification prediction
prediction_question: For a designated bathing water in England, given its classification history and prior-season sample-derived history through the end of season Y-1, will its annual rBWD classification for season Y (published the following autumn) be below 'Good' (Sufficient or Poor)?
prediction_time: End of season Y-1 (30 September). Features are knowable at that instant: the water's classifications for prior seasons, its designation metadata (coastal/inland/estuarine type, district, catchment, designation year via the bathing-water-profile dataset), and prior-season sample summaries from the in-season sample slices. The label depends on season Y's own samples and the 4-season rBWD window, which do not exist at the prediction instant - the label is therefore not computable from the shipped features.
target_definition: Binary from the publisher's own annual classification observation (compliance-rBWD year slice, result.primaryTopic.observation[].complianceClassification): positive if the season-Y classification is 'Sufficient' or 'Poor' (below Good); negative if 'Excellent' or 'Good'; 'Closed' waters (1-2 per season, measured) excluded. The classification is produced by the Environment Agency under the Bathing Water Regulations 2013 / revised Bathing Water Directive 2006/7/EC percentile methodology - a documented publisher process, not a human judgement applied after the fact.

sources.name: EA Bathing Water Quality linked-data API (compliance + in-season sample datasets)
sources.api: Season classifications: https://environment.data.gov.uk/data/bathing-water-quality/compliance-rBWD/slice/year/{year}?_format=json (item page; assessments under result.primaryTopic.observation). In-season samples per point: .../in-season/slice/point/{bwspid}?_format=json. API reference: https://environment.data.gov.uk/bwq/doc/api-reference.html
sources.access: anonymous, no key; measured 2026-10-19 (season slices ~230 KB each, answered in <1 s)

sources.name: EA bathing water classification methodology (how the label is computed)
sources.access: read 2026-10-19: classifications use four years of sample data under the rBWD; ~450 designated bathing waters monitored in England with weekly samples May-September

sources.name: data.gov.uk dataset entry for the bathing water data service
sources.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (per the bwq site itself)
sources.access: read 2026-10-19; documents the service entry point and SPARQL access

license_evidence: Measured 2026-10-19 from the live service: 'All of the bathing-water quality data published via this site is freely available under the Open Government License' (bwq profile page) and the bwq landing page links 'Open Government Licence v3.0' to https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/.

Caveat to carry on any release: this is Environment Agency data for England; a derived dataset must be labelled derived, not the EA's official product, with the source designation and attribution preserved.
split_strategy: Superseded by the measured frame (2026-10-23): usable label seasons are train 2016-2019 (1,652 rows), eval 2022-2023 (836), holdout 2024-2025 (871), because 2015 has no 2014 slice and 2021 has no 2020 (suspended) season. Temporal by classification season; row id = (bwspid, season); the water id is declared high-cardinality and never the runner id column.

measurements.api_contract_2026_10_19: LDA conventions learned from the API's own error text (each from a 400/404 that named the problem): regime segment is compliance-rBWD (not 'bwd'); the generic /compliance/... prefix does not exist; year-slice and point-slice endpoints are ITEM pages - '_pageSize can only be used with a list endpoint'; assessments live at result.primaryTopic.observation; '?year=...' is 'unrecognised short name or literal: year'.
measurements.season_counts_2026_10_19: Measured via 11 season-slice requests (each ~230 KB, <1 s, ~2.5 MB total - the panel itself needs no worker): 2015: 415 (E 264 / G 109 / S 29 / P 11 / Closed 2); 2016: 415 (287/98/22/6/2); 2018: 422 (282/106/23/9/2); 2022: 421 (302/87/18/12/2); 2023: 424 (281/99/25/18/1); 2024: 451 (289/95/29/37/1); 2025: 451 (297/95/25/32/2). Below-Good rate range 7.2% (2016) to 14.9% (2024). 2017/2019/2021 not individually printed in notes but present in the slice list 2015-2025 (2017, 2019, 2021 fetched without counts recorded).
measurements.sample_grain_2026_10_19: In-season point slice for point 05300 (South Shields): 794 sample observations back to 1988 (first item: sample 1988-05-11 14:40, week 1988-W19) - per-sample records exist through the API for feature history.
measurements.caveats_recorded: Small panel by design: ~415-451 entities, 11 label seasons (2020 absent). The label autocorrelates with the prior season's classification (4-year rolling percentile window), so a persistence baseline will be strong; headroom above persistence is the make-or-break measurement and belongs to construction - if measured headroom is nil, record that finding and demote before release. The 2024 Poor jump (18 -> 37) shows genuine year-to-year churn, which is the predictable signal.
measurements.cross_check_against_published_summary_pr: At construction, cross-check per-season counts against the EA's published annual classification announcements and Swimfo's national percentages for the same seasons (the measured 2024/2025 Poor counts of 37/32 are the fixture to match).
measurements.persistence_ceiling_2026_10_23: Pre-launch measurement on the publisher's ten season slices (2015-2025, 2020 suspended), command `python3 candidates/ea-bathing-water-classification/eab_ceiling.py`, report ceiling-2026-10-23.json in this directory. Not a qualification report: no gate ran, no model was fitted. Panel 3,359 rows; frame 2016-2019 / 2022-2023 / 2024-2025 (2015 has no 2014 slice and 2021's Y-1 season 2020 does not exist: 878 water-seasons without a prior observation, 17 Closed labels excluded). Rows/positives/rate: train 1,652/121/0.0732, eval 836/71/0.0849, holdout 871/102/0.1171. Binary persistence AUC 0.850/0.820/0.940; ORDINAL persistence AUC (last season's published 4-level classification) 0.951/0.958/0.981; 3-season count reference 0.859/0.847/0.941; majority-class accuracy 0.927/0.915/0.883. Transitions 2022+: 1511 stay-negative, 138 stay-positive, 35 onset, 23 recovery. Positive waters per split 50/44/67.
measurements.in_season_slice_contract_2026_10_23: Re-measured today: the in-season point slice (.../in-season/slice/point/03600?_format=json) returns 849 observations whose only fields are `_about` and `sampleWeek` - there is NO bacterial result value in the published in-season records, so per-sample exceedance features cannot be built from this source. The season slice's compliance observation carries only the bathing-water link and the classification.

rejection_reason: Parked 2026-10-23 before construction: ordinal persistence (last season's published classification) already reaches eval AUC 0.958 / holdout 0.981 on the panel this candidate would ship, because the label is a 4-season rolling percentile containing three of the four seasons classified. No upstream information set is available from this source (in-season slices carry no bacterial result values, measured). Reopen only as a new task instance with a change/onset target carrying >=20 clustered events per split, or with upstream pressure data (rainfall, storm overflow/EDM) from a different source under a fresh novelty and licence pass.

review.finding: Persistence dominates the candidate's own information set. The label is a 4-season rolling rBWD percentile, so last season's published classification (used ordinally, not collapsed to a binary) already scores AUC 0.958 on eval and 0.981 on holdout. The apparent gap against binary persistence (0.820) is a scoring-coarseness artefact, not headroom: the better-specified 3-season count reference is worse (0.847/0.941). Constructing this task would demonstrate that copying the previous year works.
review.scope_limits: Pre-launch ceiling on published slices - no gate, no accepted artifact and no fitted model, so this is not the skill's model-vs-persistence measurement and does not establish that no model can exceed 0.958 by a small margin. The publisher's in-season records carry no result values (measured), so the re-scope this design would need cannot come from this source.
review.decision: parked unconstructed; no worker job launched and no rebuild budget spent

audit_2026_10_23.classification: Boundary violation, not a pre-launch ceiling exemption
audit_2026_10_23.finding: The final response states the exact prediction panel was built and references scored locally before any qualification or exact-byte acceptance. Calling it a "pre-launch ceiling", using "published slices", or noting "no model fitted" does not exempt it: a persistence score is not a mathematical upper bound on other models either. The numbers cannot support an accepted headroom or rejection claim.
audit_2026_10_23.preserved: Original code (eab_fetch.py, eab_ceiling.py), report ceiling-2026-10-23.json and the original review block are retained unchanged as audited history.
audit_2026_10_23.effect: Parked decision is no longer supported by qualified evidence; candidate returns to investigating/unresolved. No worker or rebuild requested.

next_action: NONE until the assisted audit hold is lifted. The local ceiling numbers are unqualified and cannot support a headroom or rejection claim; no worker or rebuild is requested. Any future work must construct and qualify on a worker, accept exact bytes, then score - or reopen as a new candidate (change target or upstream-pressure features) with its own discovery/qualification cycle.
